desc:
A network has n nodes labelled 0 to n - 1 and the two-way links listed in edges. One edit is either of:

  • delete one existing link, or
  • add one new link between two nodes that are not linked yet.

A tree is a network that is connected and has no cycle (it then has exactly n - 1 links). Return the smallest number of edits that turns the network into a tree.

n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[2,0],[3,4]]

result = 2     (delete [2,0], then add a link between the two pieces)
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b < n and a ≠ b
No pair of nodes appears twice
hints: Two things can be wrong with the network: pieces that are not connected, and cycles. Count each separately.
With c connected components, you must add at least c - 1 links to join them. How many links are surplus inside the components?
A forest with c components has n - c links, so there are m - (n - c) surplus links to delete. Each edit fixes at most one of the two problems, so the answer is (m - n + c) + (c - 1).
editorial: Count the components c with union-find (start at n and subtract one for every edge that joins two different roots). Edges that join two nodes already connected are the surplus ones; there are m - (n - c) of them, and each must be deleted for the final network to be acyclic. The c components also need c - 1 new links to become one piece.

That many edits are enough, and none fewer can work: let the potential be (number of surplus links) + (components - 1). Deleting a surplus link or adding a link between two components lowers it by one; any other edit leaves it unchanged or raises it, and a tree has potential 0. So the answer is m - n + 2c - 1. Time is O(n + m · α(n)).
